requirements.name: per-surface-material
requirements.message:
`pcba:mesh:matClass` (`plastic metal ceramic solder mask copper silkscreen other`) names a
mesh's material class alongside its bound material. It MUST be authored explicitly on `pkg_*`
and `fixture_*` meshes, whose material is genuinely ambiguous. On `board_*` meshes it **derives
from the role** and need not be authored; any authored value must match the derivation.This page follows PCBA to USD Input Contract **1.0.2**, section 9.

requirements.name: pin-pitch
requirements.message:
`pcba:component:pinPitchMm` (a float, in millimetres) gives the centre-to-centre
spacing between adjacent contacts. It is required when meaningful and is omitted
for 2-terminal passives.

requirements.name: anchor
requirements.message:
The component asset root MUST sit at a declared anchor named by
`pcba:component:anchor` (`body_centroid`, `pin1`, `footprint_origin`, or
`mesh_origin`). `pcba:component:bodyCentroidLocal` and `pcba:mesh:originOffset`
together give deterministic placement when the mesh origin is off the body.

requirements.name: markings
requirements.message:
`pcba:component:markings` (a string) records the visible marking text on the
component. It is required when markings are present and is the ground truth for
OCR and wrong-part inspection.

requirements.name: polarity
requirements.message:
`pcba:component:polarityType` (a token) names how a polarized part indicates its
polarity. It is required for polarized parts and is the ground truth for
reverse-polarity defects. Pin-1 / polarity / marking features MUST be authored as
**standalone geometry** (`pkg_marking`), never baked into a texture.

requirements.name: body-height
requirements.message:
Every electrical component MUST carry `pcba:component:heightMm` (the Z extent of the
component in millimetres, greater than zero). The body mesh should also carry a standard USD
`extent`, which the board-side geometric cross-checks rely on. Together they provide height and
world-bounds ground truth.This page follows PCBA to USD Input Contract **1.0.2**, section 8.

requirements.name: pin1-position
requirements.message:
`pcba:component:pin1PosMm` (a `point3f`) gives the actual offset of pin 1 from the
component anchor. It is required for keyed or orientation-sensitive parts and is
the ground truth for pin-1 orientation defects.

requirements.name: pin-geometry
requirements.message:
Every pin prim MUST carry `pcba:pin:number` — a stable id, **unique within the component** — and
`pcba:pin:solderable` (`bool`: does this contact form a solder joint?). `pcba:pin:crossSection`,
`pcba:pin:terminalType`, and `pcba:pin:designator` are OPTIONAL and validated when authored.
The board side never authors `pcba:pin:number`: a pad or barrel names a pin with
`pcba:board:componentPinNumber`.This page follows PCBA to USD Input Contract **1.0.2**, section 10.

requirements.name: nominal-appearance
requirements.message:
Every component MUST carry a representative nominal appearance:
`pcba:component:bodyColorNominal` (a `color3f`), `pcba:component:finishNominal` (a
token: `matte`, `gloss`, `metallic`, `other`), and
`pcba:component:materialClassNominal` (a token: `plastic`, `metal`, `ceramic`,
`solder`, `other`).

requirements.name: press-fit-state
requirements.message:
A `press_fit` part is a solderless through-hole part: its holes are plated, its barrels are
real and required, and the camera looks down them. Which of its contacts take solder — and
therefore which solder-defect classes apply — is determined **per pin** by `pcba:pin:solderable`,
not by the part-level process class.This page follows PCBA to USD Input Contract **1.0.2**, sections 6, 10 and 12.

requirements.name: pin-count
requirements.message:
Every electrical component MUST carry `pcba:component:pinCount` (an integer, greater than
zero), and it MUST equal the number of pin prims on the component. It is the contact enumeration the
solder simulation relies on.

requirements.name: placement
requirements.message:
Every placed component prim MUST carry `pcba:component:side` (`top` \| `bottom`). Electrical
parts MUST also carry `pcba:component:nominalPosMm` (board-local x, y in mm) and
`pcba:component:nominalRotationDeg` (rotation about the board normal Z). For `fiducial` and
`mechanical` placements the pose fields are SHOULD.This page follows PCBA to USD Input Contract **1.0.2**, sections 8 and 8.1.
